data.why: The repo's own examples/candidates.csv (trastuzumab, adalimumab, a liability-rich variant) is the batch-upload demo; one nanobody-only (VHH, no VL) row was added to exercise the single-chain path the UI also supports.

goals: Paste a VH+VL (or VHH) sequence and get a CDR-aware liability scan with exact residue sites
See biophysical risk axes (hydrophobicity, charge, pI, charge asymmetry, CDR lengths) flagged green/amber/red against 1,093 clinical-stage antibodies
Get an overall developability composite score as a pre-flight check before committing lab resources
Batch-upload a CSV of candidates and rank them by developability score
Get ranked mutation suggestions that clear a flagged liability without regressing the score or touching CDR3
Run the redesign loop to apply a safe combination of fixes together and compare before/after reports

review.summary: The tree captures Sentinel's purpose well: triage antibody Fv candidates against the clinical distribution, then repair flagged liabilities with scored point mutations and a safe redesign. The evidence I checked largely matches what the nodes claim. Before filing it needs a few fixes: one mislabeled general task, a deployment step presented as a science phase, a misplaced validation task, PDF export wrongly recorded as broken, several weak screen citations, and missing VHH and permalink paths.
